After a successful connector response, the current session should receive the documented `playwriter_*` tool surface on the next turn so it can enumerate only user-approved tabs.

The configured Playwright MCP is disabled, and no Playwright process is active. The Playwriter relay is live and reports version 0.5.0, so this does not appear to be a conflict with Playwright's isolated MCP.

title: Bug: secret inventory invalid names trigger an unbound cleanup variable
body:
## What

Make `aidevops secret inventory` handle an invalid discovered secret name without cascading into an `unbound variable` failure. The command should either support valid nested backend paths or report/skip invalid entries deterministically, then complete cleanup safely.

## Why

During an interactive NVIDIA provider setup, the inventory command discovered a slash-containing backend entry and emitted:

```text
Invalid secret inventory name
names_file: unbound variable
```

No secret value was read or exposed. The second error obscures the actionable validation failure and aborts inventory, preventing users from auditing which secure keys are configured.

## Evidence and likely cause

- Current `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` initializes `local names_file=""`, assigns it with `mktemp`, and installs `trap 'rm -f "$names_file"' EXIT` around lines 600-604.
- Discovered gopass names flow through `inventory_add_name ... "$names_file"` around lines 615 and 640.
- `inventory_add_name` rejects an invalid name around lines 669-674.
- When that rejection returns from the inventory function and the shell later exits under nounset, the EXIT trap expands a function-local variable that is no longer in scope, producing the observed `names_file: unbound variable` error.

## Expected implementation

- Make temporary-file cleanup independent of an out-of-scope local variable.
- Define and test the intended policy for slash-containing/nested backend names: normalize/support them when valid, or skip/report them without aborting the complete inventory.
- Preserve strict validation for environment-variable-facing secret names and never print secret values.

## Targets

- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`
- Existing secret-helper tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`; add a focused regression covering an invalid or nested discovered name with nounset enabled.

## Verification

- Run the focused secret-helper test suite.
- Run ShellCheck on changed shell files with zero violations.
- Reproduce inventory against a fixture containing a slash-bearing discovered entry and verify: no `unbound variable`, no secret value output, deterministic exit/result, and temporary files removed.

## Pre-flight

- Memory recall: session-specific query returned no prior fix for this defect.
- Discovery: upstream issue search for `secret inventory` found no matching open or closed report.
- File refs: all target references above were verified at current `main`.
- Tier: `tier:standard` because the cleanup defect is bounded, but the nested-name compatibility policy needs implementation judgment.
- Seeded draft PR: skipped; issue-only evidence is sufficient and no canonical checkout edits are allowed.

title: Exclude upstream-only changes from pending runtime-risk classification
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Prevent pre-commit runtime-risk validation from classifying upstream-only changes as part of a local PR when the worktree is behind its remote base. Preserve fail-closed validation of actual local changes before Git mutation and final-diff validation after rebase.

## Why / observed evidence

While delivering documentation PR #31295 for issue #31288, `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --risk-level low --testing-level self-assessed` stopped before staging with `Critical runtime risk requires runtime-verified evidence; PR body generation blocked.` The actual local change comprised 15 Markdown files. `git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main` reported `0 11`; `git diff --name-only origin/main -- .agents/scripts` listed 24 upstream-only script/test paths, including dispatch, worker-token and release-provenance code. No such code was locally edited. After a normal scoped commit and rebase, the identical documentation patch passed the same gate. `git range-diff` confirmed patch equality. The shipped documentation PR deliberately did not change this helper.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Current implementation inspected: `_pending_runtime_files_changed` compares the worktree directly with the remote tip using `git diff --name-only "$base_ref"`, then includes untracked files. `_validate_pending_runtime_metadata` also passes that remote base into diff classification.
- [x] Collision discovery found the originating prevalidation change associated with GH#30939, but no open related fix. Broad keyword search results were unrelated historical PRs; deduplicate again before implementation.
- [x] Target paths and existing test harness verified.
- [x] Tier: thinking, because this changes the full-loop safety/dispatch path. No change to runtime-verification requirements is authorised.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped: this is a separate corrective task, not part of the already merged documentation change.

## Files Scope

Canonicalized from the two existing edit targets below; the read-only reference is not an added write permission.

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh`: prospective file set, comparison baseline and keyword diff context.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`: extend existing focused coverage.
- Read-only reference: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`, where `_validate_pending_runtime_metadata` must remain before `_stage_and_commit` and final validation remains after rebase.

## How

Use the existing conservative risk derivation and pending WORKTREE target contracts. Resolve a comparison baseline that captures this branch's committed, staged, unstaged and untracked changes without treating incoming upstream-only changes as local deletions/modifications. Apply the same ownership boundary to the file list and diff-content classification. Preserve fail-closed behaviour when baseline resolution is unknown. Do not move validation after commit, downgrade genuine sensitive code, or trust a caller-supplied low-risk declaration.

## Acceptance criteria

- Behind-base documentation-only work remains Low/self-assessed even when upstream added sensitive runtime code.
- Genuine local auth/credential/high-risk runtime changes, including untracked files and local commits, still require substantive runtime-verified evidence before staging/commit.
- Staged and unstaged changes remain represented, and final post-rebase validation still catches actual final-diff risk.
- Missing/invalid comparison refs remain fail-closed; no user data or Git state is mutated by prevalidation.
- Cover upstream-only paths, local runtime changes, and comparison-context consistency in the existing focused harness, without new test infrastructure.

## Verification and rollback

Run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`, scoped ShellCheck, and `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`. Use disposable Git fixtures in the existing harness; do not reproduce by modifying canonical checkouts or live repositories. Verify rejected cases do not stage, commit, push, or create PRs. Roll back with a follow-up revert PR; never bypass the gate or fabricate runtime evidence.

This issue authorises its normal automatic dispatch; the completed documentation PR is not blocked by this follow-up.

title: Keep scope and integration blocker recovery owned by AI
body:
# AI-owned scope and integration blocker recovery

Tracking issue: #31305.

## What

Keep ordinary implementation blockers owned by workers and Pulse until a verified outcome or a genuine human-only decision. Provide bounded delegated authority to correct incomplete briefs, coordinate adjacent integration work, and continue preserved work without requiring a new interactive session.

## Why

In #31265 a worker stopped because the shared claim helper needed for the requested outcome was absent from Files Scope. Another attempt preserved draft PR #31269 but still deferred the same integration boundary. The user explicitly authorises a systemic fix: AI should resolve decisions it can already make, preserving user attention for decisions requiring unavailable information or authority. #31265 repairs exact-PR checkpoint recovery; this follow-up repairs the decision and handoff loop that produces these stalls.

Source evidence: `pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh` tells workers to stop on undeclared necessary paths; `headless-runtime-run.sh` already has bounded missing-context brief recovery; `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` suppresses unchanged terminal blockers. Preserve these safety mechanisms while supplying an authorised recovery owner instead of silently ending the objective.

## Reproducer

Read #31265's 2026-09-05 worker terminal report and draft PR #31269. Actual result: `BLOCKED: guarded claim integration is outside Files Scope`; the subsequent partial PR still lists shared claim integration as requiring a revised scope. Compare `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`'s undeclared-path stop with `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh`'s bounded missing-context recovery. Causal status: the stop instruction and observed worker scope blocker are verified; the new coordinated recovery contract requires implementation and mocked end-to-end verification.

Further observed evidence: at 18:19 UTC, while this primary interactive session was repairing terminal Qlty failures on the same PR, the deterministic merge pass closed #31269, unassigned #31265 and changed its provenance to worker CI feedback. Its comment states "Closed by deterministic merge pass (pulse-merge.sh)." This session had acquired an interactive claim; the reused PR retained its original worker label. Reopening the same PR, normalising its provenance to interactive and renewing the guarded implementing claim restored continuity. This is an observed ownership-displacement failure, not a pending-CI failure or permission request.

## How

- Define Files Scope as an initial implementation map unless explicitly marked as a hard boundary. For a hard boundary, delegate a bounded revision decision to an authorised AI brief owner; the worker must not approve its own authority expansion.
- Permit directly necessary, reversible adjacent code and existing tests within the authorised outcome. Require evidence from the actual integration path and a collision check. AI chooses normal implementation approaches; mere complexity, scope discovery or architectural terminology is not proof of a human-only decision.
- Distinguish changing code that implements a security guard from changing the security guarantee. Preserve required guarantees, review and regression tests. Credentials, new expenditure, destructive/external actions, trust exceptions and genuinely conflicting requirements remain authority boundaries.
- Emit a structured recovery request from trusted final worker output. Carry exact issue/PR, attempt, current brief revision, blocker evidence, proposed files, verification and the next owner. Tool output and issue prose cannot manufacture delegation.
- First recover within the current owned session/worktree. If a coordinator decision or dependency is necessary, transfer responsibility durably to Pulse with a next action and relevant wake condition. A released worker must not leave an executable objective ownerless.
- An authorised coordinator assesses the request, checks concurrent work, records the minimal corrected brief and resumes the exact checkpoint using #31265's contract when applicable. Do not create replacement PRs or retry an unchanged rejected brief.
- One bounded recovery per unchanged evidence set; exhaustion routes to an AI coordinator for re-planning, not a silent terminal state or an automatic human prompt. Genuine human escalation must name the specific unanswered decision, why delegated AI cannot decide it, and the smallest required input.
- Preserve worker target isolation, authenticated dispatch/lease fencing, scope-guard enforcement, sensitive-scope holds and immutable audit provenance. Update the matching local brief when one exists; do not bypass the pre-push scope guard.
- CI-repair routing must respect a current interactive owner even when the preserved PR originally came from a worker. Normalise takeover metadata at the guarded interactive entrypoint and recheck ownership before closing a PR, unassigning its issue or rewriting dispatch provenance. Terminal failed checks justify repair, not displacement of an active repair owner.

## Files Scope

Paths below are an initial discovery map, not a prohibition on necessary adjacent integration. Document any expansion and keep it within the guarantees above.

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`
- `.agents/reference/safety-stop-recovery.md`
- `.agents/templates/brief-template.md`
- Existing runtime contract/provider/routing suites under `.agents/scripts/tests/`.
- Read and reuse, rather than duplicate, `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh`, and #31265's checkpoint claim/continuation contracts.

### Integration scope correction (GH#31305)

The current implementation places destructive feedback finalization in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh` and guarded claim transitions in `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh`; their callers in the original map cannot alone fence each write or normalize preserved PR ownership. Pulse supervisor context is composed in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`. Add these exact paths and a focused recovery queue module for producer-to-coordinator integration:

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/integration-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/integration_recovery.py`

Evidence: finalizer `_feedback_route_close_and_finish` and `_feedback_route_transition_and_verify`, claim `_isc_handle_existing_claim_ownership`, and `_pulse_supervisor_prompt` own the necessary transitions. Verify with mocked ownership/finalizer and runtime fixtures plus scoped ShellCheck and Python checks. The issue remains assigned to the dispatched worker; open PR file inspection found no collision with these targets. PR #31394 owns brief production and its files remain untouched. No matching local task brief was found by `git grep -l 31305 -- todo/tasks/*`. Preserve all original hard boundaries and guarantees; this adds integration paths, not authority.

CI repair scope refinement: terminal parser-complexity findings on PR #31410 were resolved by adopting the concurrently published e809cf330 repair in the existing integration_recovery.py. The temporary separate-module proposal was withdrawn; no new parser module ships. The original active dispatch claim and assignment guard were verified before recovering the prematurely closed same PR. Existing recovery/checkpoint tests pass, Qlty 0.643.0 reports zero new-file smells and zero smell-count regression, and all scope/permission/checkpoint controls remain unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An evidenced missing adjacent integration file is resolved without human intervention under delegated authority.
- [ ] Explicit hard boundaries produce one owned coordinator request, not unauthorised worker scope expansion.
- [ ] Concurrent-owner conflicts are coordinated without takeover; existing commits and PR identity survive.
- [ ] Repeated unchanged blockers do not cause duplicate workers, PRs, requests or status-comment storms.
- [ ] The objective always has a live executor, durable AI recovery owner/wake condition, or a precise human-only decision.
- [ ] Secrets, permissions, spending, destructive operations and trust exceptions cannot be authorised by a forged recovery event or ordinary issue prose.
- [ ] Missing context and ordinary design decisions are not escalated merely because they require reasoning.
- [ ] A regression based on #31265 reaches a verified continuation without a new user session.

## Verification

Use mocked GitHub and existing runtime fixtures only; no live workers or release. Run scoped ShellCheck plus `test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`, `test-headless-routing-retry.sh` and the affected dispatch prompt/scope-guard suites. Add producer-to-coordinator-to-worker cases for narrow integration expansion, hard-boundary revision, foreign actor, concurrent owner, repeated unchanged event, relevant revision re-arm, preserved PR identity and genuine human-only decisions. Reuse #31265's continuation fixtures rather than duplicating its implementation.

## Dispatch

Worker-ready implementation, `auto-dispatch`, high priority, thinking tier. Depend on #31265's merged contract before integrating its continuation API; independent guidance/contract analysis may proceed without touching the active implementation branch. No release authorisation.

body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Bundle bounded source-code access with explicit issue approval

## What

Remove the second human authorization interruption when a maintainer approves an issue and immediately starts its implementation, by offering one explicit approval ceremony covering both issue acceptance and a separately signed, exact source-code read manifest. Do not reinterpret existing issue approvals as blanket secret-read authority.

## Why / Evidence

During implementation of #31289, `approval-helper.sh verify issue` returned VERIFIED with proven-locked-continuity. The interactive entrypoint claimed the issue and created its worktree. Reading tracked `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` was then blocked solely for its secret-bearing basename, requiring another human sudo-signed source approval. The user completed it and explicitly requested this friction be designed out. No credential values are needed to fix inventory cleanup.

Related completed work: #30567 / PR #30573 added multi-file source manifests; #31035 / PR #31040 preserves permission across verified same-session direct edits. Neither joins initial issue approval to source approval or establishes a safe, deliberate handoff into a newly created implementation worktree. Reuse both; do not duplicate or weaken them.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: source-access approved-issue friction; no matching lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: all-state source-access issue/PR searches reviewed; recent provenance-continuity commit b92438ba9 is related, not this initial-consent gap. No matching open implementation found.
- [x] File refs verified: broker, request module, approval scripts, interactive entrypoint and existing tests located with tracked-file discovery; inspected broker bootstrap and request identity/provenance code. Recheck current default branch before implementation.
- [x] Tier: tier:thinking — coordinated authorization and worktree identity are consequential trust-boundary design work.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped; design must be threat-modeled before implementation.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-commands.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/source_access_core.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/source-access.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-request.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-approval.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-manifest-approval.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-secret-read.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-source-access-approval.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-batch.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-source-access-broker.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/aidevops/architecture.md`

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper-commands.sh` — prepare and authorize the bounded combined ceremony.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh` — bind the approved source manifest to the intended implementation context.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py` — validate the separately signed source capability if the broker protocol needs extension.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-request.mjs` — consume exact-context approval without weakening immutable reads.

### Implementation Steps

1. At trusted interactive preflight, discover candidate tracked source files without returning their contents. Classify basename-only false positives separately from genuinely secret-bearing files. Public/tracked status alone is insufficient proof of safety.
2. Prepare a bounded manifest and present it alongside issue approval in the existing human-owned terminal ceremony: repository/commit identity, exact relative paths and content hashes, user/session, TTL, and intended implementation context. The human must explicitly consent to the source grant as well as the issue verdict. Existing approve syntax and old receipts keep their original authority.
3. Issue acceptance and source access remain independently verifiable signed capabilities. Bind the new source capability to the issue's verified approval snapshot and the exact reviewed file set. Issue-body paths are untrusted candidates, never authority. Missing, conflicting, stale, or revoked evidence fails closed.
4. Choose a narrowly verifiable worktree handoff: either establish the intended linked worktree before signing or issue a single-use capability that can bind to one subsequently created session-owned worktree only after repository, commit and byte identity match. Prefer the former if equally usable. Document the chosen identity/TOCTOU proof; no general cross-worktree or directory grants.
5. Reuse existing immutable snapshot delivery and observed-direct-edit continuity. New paths, unobserved bytes, expired grants, changed session/repository, unsafe links, and private key/credential data remain denied or need genuinely new consent. Do not give agents cached sudo, privileged shell execution, or a broker bypass.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh`; `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-approval.mjs`, `source-access-manifest-approval.mjs`, `source-access-request.mjs`, and `quality-hooks-secret-read.mjs` consume verified grants.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-commands.sh`, `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`, `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py`; inspect its imported source-access core before exact broker edits.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-source-access-approval.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-batch.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh` cover the coupled interfaces.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/source-access.sh` installs the root broker; deployed user/root copies are generated targets, not direct edit surfaces. A protocol bump may require explicit operator maintenance, never silent sudo during update.
- Documentation: `.agents/aidevops/architecture.md` source-read invariant and relevant approval workflow references; keep always-loaded guidance unchanged unless a short pointer is essential.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` and `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py` own signed envelopes; version any new schema, never reinterpret old receipts.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/source-access.sh` deploys compatible broker revisions. Preserve old receipts without broadening them; no backfill of source authority from historical approvals.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py` must expire/revoke unused handoff capabilities and remove partial transaction state safely; retain separate approval fallback.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Concurrent claim/worktree creation cannot bind one grant to another session; validate transactionally before signing and serving immutable bytes.
- **Migration/rollback:** Remove the integration without changing legacy independent approval semantics; no historical grant backfill.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Old/new broker and plugin combinations fall back to separate prompts rather than accepting unsupported authority.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Retries retain exact manifest identity and cannot duplicate a one-use handoff or broaden granted paths.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Report issue accepted/source missing accurately; resume only the original manifest or discard unused partial state safely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A fixture matching #31289 requires one explicit human ceremony for issue plus eligible source manifest, then can read the exact source in the intended worktree and perform supported verified direct-edit/read cycles without a second prompt.
- [ ] Legacy issue-only approval cannot read protected source. Real credentials/private keys, untracked or substituted content, extra paths, symlink/hard-link changes, stale/revoked/expired signatures, another user/session/repo/worktree and replayed handoffs are denied.
- [ ] Failures and cancellation cannot produce a partial grant represented as complete, broaden authority, or expose credential values. Retrying safely resumes only the originally reviewed manifest.
- [ ] Existing separate approval commands remain supported; documentation explains when a fresh prompt is legitimate versus redundant.
- [ ] Security review explicitly validates trust roots, worktree binding, atomicity, TOCTOU safety, and mixed-version rollback before merge.

### Verification Before Dispatch

Commands to run during implementation (not claimed run for this brief):

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-source-access-approval.mjs
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-batch.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-source-access-broker.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** Node tests prove immutable delivery and provenance; Python covers signed manifest identity/revocation; batch/interactive tests prove one-ceremony UX and claim/worktree binding; setup tests prove mixed-version broker deployment. **Parent issue:** #31265 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. **Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` is also mandatory. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #31265:**

```bash
gh issue comment 31265 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31265 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31265 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31265 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
```

Make canonical aggregation-successor refresh accept a tagless reserved lane's PR-only intent by resolving it against the existing reviewed manifest, and parse normal Markdown signature dividers without silently losing terminal trailers.

## Reproducer

For PR-body Markdown parsing, use the appropriate interpret-trailers no-divider mode while retaining exact raw/parsed identity/source matching and strict terminal-block validation. title: Distinguish missing successor refs from GitHub error payloads

## What

Create a missing successor branch only after a verified GitHub 404, and never treat an HTTP error body as an existing branch SHA.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: current committed `full-loop-release-helper.sh refresh-aggregate 31320` after the reserved-intent fix.

title: Make session handoffs actionable and prevent premature stops in authorized work
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Make incomplete-session handoffs actionable and preserve authorized execution

## What

Fix shared aidevops session/full-loop guidance so all users receive a clear next-action owner, accurate completion state, and durable continuation instead of explanatory plans that prematurely end authorized work. This is the systemic communication counterpart to #31311, not a local memory preference.

## Why

Observed during #31289/#31290: after the user explicitly requested full-loop through release, the assistant repeatedly described next steps without executing or identifying a required human action. It called the session a safe stopping point while the release remained incomplete, and repeatedly regenerated expired approval requests. The user explicitly stated communication success belongs to the sender and requested systemic fixes. #31311 owns the approval mechanism; this issue owns cross-runtime execution and handoff behavior. No release was verified in that interaction.

## Reproducer

Observed interaction on aidevops 3.32.316 in OpenCode 1.18.29:
1. Authorize issues #31289 and #31290 with "approved. full-loop through to release please".
2. Encounter a source-read permission blocker and indeterminate remote merge evidence while a separate systemic repair remains available.
3. Ask "all done for this session?" and "what do we do next?".
4. Actual response described a safe stopping point and returned a multi-step plan rather than executing available work or giving an explicit human-only action. The release remained unpublished and the promised second systemic issue remained unfiled until the user challenged it.
5. Expected response distinguishes incomplete delivery from completed work, executes authorized safe next steps, and preserves a verified continuation before any unavoidable pause. This is an observed model-behavior failure, not a claim that every model run deterministically reproduces it; validate with the behavioral cases below.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory/context: the concrete user corrections and unfinished PR #31302 establish the failure; local memory alone is not delivery.
- [x] Discovery: open communication/continuation search found no issue; premature-completion search returned broader #31280 and #31294, not this specific contract. Open completion-policy PR search found none. Recheck history and those broad tasks before implementation; coordinate any overlapping guidance edits.
- [x] File refs verified: session/safety-stop/full-loop command and existing session-completion policy test are tracked; inspected test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh, whose assertions protect summary phrasing but do not prove execution behavior.
- [x] Tier: tier:standard — bounded shared guidance and existing policy coverage, not a new lifecycle engine.
- [x] Seed: skipped; preserve existing guidance and determine smallest conflict repair first.

## Files Scope

Canonicalized from the existing four EDIT declarations below; no new write paths or authority are added.

- `.agents/reference/session.md`
- `.agents/reference/safety-stop-recovery.md`
- `.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` — tracked canonical target of the command symlink; verify with `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh`, `shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh`, and `git diff --check`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh`

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/reference/session.md` — define explicit next-action ownership and truthful stopping states.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/safety-stop-recovery.md` — actionable durable handoff when a human-only gate blocks progress.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md` — align command behavior with continued ownership and safe recovery.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh` — extend existing shared policy regression checks.

### Implementation Steps

1. Read current session/full-loop/safety-stop guidance and recent history; identify contradictory or missing clauses rather than appending repeated instructions. Reuse existing completion and continuation contracts.
2. Establish three explicit outcomes: completed with verified evidence; blocked on an identified external dependency; active with an actual running/resumable executor. A plan is neither execution nor a running worker. Never imply that work continues after a final response without a real mechanism.
3. While authorized safe work remains, execute it instead of asking the user to approve the same plan or advising session closure. A safety gate pauses its unsafe path, not independent safe work. Honor explicit user stop requests and do not bypass permissions.
4. Human-only handoffs state action required, exact durable action, what it unblocks, and how completion will be verified. Otherwise say no user action is required and accurately explain who owns continuation. Do not assume immediate attendance or repeat expired commands; link #31311 for the mechanism.
5. Before any unavoidable pause, persist goal, preserved user directions, issue/PR/worktree identity, verified outcomes, all unmet criteria, blockers, next executable steps, and resume conditions using existing checkpoint machinery. Verify the checkpoint exists. Never mark an incomplete full-loop complete merely because a checkpoint exists.
6. Extend the existing policy test and add compact behavioral examples to the owning reference document: authorized pending work, human-only permission, recoverable API failure, delayed attendance, genuine completed delivery, explicit user stop. Review each against the contract; literal tests alone do not prove model compliance.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/reference/session.md`, `.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md`; check `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` for duplicated/linked lifecycle guidance before editing.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** shared Markdown guidance and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh`; no GitHub merge or permission semantics change.
- **Tests/fixtures:** existing session-completion policy test, plus behavioral examples within `.agents/reference/session.md`; use existing full-loop completion evidence tests if lifecycle logic is touched.
- **Schemas/config:** reuse the documented checkpoint contract in `.agents/reference/session.md`; no new state store or automatic model-output classifier.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** setup deploys canonical `.agents/` guidance to runtime installations. Edit repository sources, never deployed mirrors; verify cross-runtime guidance references remain effective.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/reference/session.md` retains existing checkpoint format; no stored-data migration because only guidance and policy coverage change.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert `.agents/reference/session.md` and the companion policy-test change while preserving live worktrees and checkpoint artifacts. No cleanup permission expansion.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** checkpoints retain exact session/worktree ownership; do not overwrite another session's state or duplicate an active worker.
- **Migration/rollback:** reuse current checkpoint semantics; revert guidance without deleting persisted continuation.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** old runtimes retain existing lifecycle format; no new required protocol or always-loaded size increase.
- **Idempotency/retry:** resume from verified state, not repeated reviews/approval prompts or duplicated issue creation.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** checkpoint failures must be surfaced; never claim durable recovery unless persistence is verified. API/permission failures stay distinct from failed product checks.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh
git diff --check
```

- **Surface mapping:** policy test protects canonical shared instruction presence and contradictions; ShellCheck validates the existing test; diff check catches malformed edits. Review the six behavioral examples explicitly and record expected next-action owner, allowed continuation and truthful stopping state. Run existing changed-Markdown lint and required CI; do not claim a literal guard proves future model behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Shared guidance reaches supported runtimes and provides the same unambiguous next-action/continuation contract without a personal-memory dependency.
- [ ] An authorized unfinished task is not called complete or handed back as another plan when safe execution is available; explicit user stop and genuine safety gates remain respected.
- [ ] A human-only blocker yields one actionable durable handoff; no short-lived-command retry loop or claim of background progress without a live executor.
- [ ] Every unavoidable pause preserves all unmet commitments and exact resume steps in a verified checkpoint; delivered/blocked/active states are distinguishable.
- [ ] Existing summary/cleanup policy tests remain green; new coverage and six reviewed behavioral examples demonstrate the intended contract and its limits.

## Dispatch

User explicitly requested a systemic implementation issue. Auto-dispatch, tier:standard. Keep independent of #31311's broker changes; reference it but do not block useful guidance delivery on its completion. No publication authority is included in this brief.

## Consolidation target: #31311

**Parent issue:** #31311 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** Reduce approved-issue source-access friction with bounded combined consent
**Parent labels:** `enhancement,status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:interactive,consolidation-in-progress`

> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #31311 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` is also mandatory. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #31311:**

```bash
gh issue comment 31311 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31311 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31311 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31311 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #31311** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn

# Bundle bounded source-code access with explicit issue approval

## What

Remove the second human authorization interruption when a maintainer approves an issue and immediately starts its implementation, by offering one explicit approval ceremony covering both issue acceptance and a separately signed, exact source-code read manifest. Do not reinterpret existing issue approvals as blanket secret-read authority.

## Why / Evidence

During implementation of #31289, `approval-helper.sh verify issue` returned VERIFIED with proven-locked-continuity. The interactive entrypoint claimed the issue and created its worktree. Reading tracked `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` was then blocked solely for its secret-bearing basename, requiring another human sudo-signed source approval. The user completed it and explicitly requested this friction be designed out. No credential values are needed to fix inventory cleanup.

Related completed work: #30567 / PR #30573 added multi-file source manifests; #31035 / PR #31040 preserves permission across verified same-session direct edits. Neither joins initial issue approval to source approval or establishes a safe, deliberate handoff into a newly created implementation worktree. Reuse both; do not duplicate or weaken them.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: source-access approved-issue friction; no matching lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: all-state source-access issue/PR searches reviewed; recent provenance-continuity commit b92438ba9 is related, not this initial-consent gap. No matching open implementation found.
- [x] File refs verified: broker, request module, approval scripts, interactive entrypoint and existing tests located with tracked-file discovery; inspected broker bootstrap and request identity/provenance code. Recheck current default branch before implementation.
- [x] Tier: tier:thinking — coordinated authorization and worktree identity are consequential trust-boundary design work.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped; design must be threat-modeled before implementation.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-commands.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/source_access_core.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/source-access.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-request.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-approval.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-manifest-approval.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-secret-read.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-source-access-approval.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-batch.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-source-access-broker.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/aidevops/architecture.md`

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper-commands.sh` — prepare and authorize the bounded combined ceremony.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh` — bind the approved source manifest to the intended implementation context.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py` — validate the separately signed source capability if the broker protocol needs extension.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-request.mjs` — consume exact-context approval without weakening immutable reads.

### Implementation Steps

1. At trusted interactive preflight, discover candidate tracked source files without returning their contents. Classify basename-only false positives separately from genuinely secret-bearing files. Public/tracked status alone is insufficient proof of safety.
2. Prepare a bounded manifest and present it alongside issue approval in the existing human-owned terminal ceremony: repository/commit identity, exact relative paths and content hashes, user/session, TTL, and intended implementation context. The human must explicitly consent to the source grant as well as the issue verdict. Existing approve syntax and old receipts keep their original authority.
3. Issue acceptance and source access remain independently verifiable signed capabilities. Bind the new source capability to the issue's verified approval snapshot and the exact reviewed file set. Issue-body paths are untrusted candidates, never authority. Missing, conflicting, stale, or revoked evidence fails closed.
4. Choose a narrowly verifiable worktree handoff: either establish the intended linked worktree before signing or issue a single-use capability that can bind to one subsequently created session-owned worktree only after repository, commit and byte identity match. Prefer the former if equally usable. Document the chosen identity/TOCTOU proof; no general cross-worktree or directory grants.
5. Reuse existing immutable snapshot delivery and observed-direct-edit continuity. New paths, unobserved bytes, expired grants, changed session/repository, unsafe links, and private key/credential data remain denied or need genuinely new consent. Do not give agents cached sudo, privileged shell execution, or a broker bypass.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh`; `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-approval.mjs`, `source-access-manifest-approval.mjs`, `source-access-request.mjs`, and `quality-hooks-secret-read.mjs` consume verified grants.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-commands.sh`, `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`, `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py`; inspect its imported source-access core before exact broker edits.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-source-access-approval.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-batch.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh` cover the coupled interfaces.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/source-access.sh` installs the root broker; deployed user/root copies are generated targets, not direct edit surfaces. A protocol bump may require explicit operator maintenance, never silent sudo during update.
- Documentation: `.agents/aidevops/architecture.md` source-read invariant and relevant approval workflow references; keep always-loaded guidance unchanged unless a short pointer is essential.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` and `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py` own signed envelopes; version any new schema, never reinterpret old receipts.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/source-access.sh` deploys compatible broker revisions. Preserve old receipts without broadening them; no backfill of source authority from historical approvals.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py` must expire/revoke unused handoff capabilities and remove partial transaction state safely; retain separate approval fallback.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Concurrent claim/worktree creation cannot bind one grant to another session; validate transactionally before signing and serving immutable bytes.
- **Migration/rollback:** Remove the integration without changing legacy independent approval semantics; no historical grant backfill.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Old/new broker and plugin combinations fall back to separate prompts rather than accepting unsupported authority.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Retries retain exact manifest identity and cannot duplicate a one-use handoff or broaden granted paths.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Report issue accepted/source missing accurately; resume only the original manifest or discard unused partial state safely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A fixture matching #31289 requires one explicit human ceremony for issue plus eligible source manifest, then can read the exact source in the intended worktree and perform supported verified direct-edit/read cycles without a second prompt.
- [ ] Legacy issue-only approval cannot read protected source. Real credentials/private keys, untracked or substituted content, extra paths, symlink/hard-link changes, stale/revoked/expired signatures, another user/session/repo/worktree and replayed handoffs are denied.
- [ ] Failures and cancellation cannot produce a partial grant represented as complete, broaden authority, or expose credential values. Retrying safely resumes only the originally reviewed manifest.
- [ ] Existing separate approval commands remain supported; documentation explains when a fresh prompt is legitimate versus redundant.
- [ ] Security review explicitly validates trust roots, worktree binding, atomicity, TOCTOU safety, and mixed-version rollback before merge.

### Verification Before Dispatch

Commands to run during implementation (not claimed run for this brief):

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-source-access-approval.mjs
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-batch.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-source-access-broker.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** Node tests prove immutable delivery and provenance; Python covers signed manifest identity/revocation; batch/interactive tests prove one-ceremony UX and claim/worktree binding; setup tests prove mixed-version broker deployment. Run changed-file ShellCheck and the existing Python/JS lint, then required CI. Use fake keys, repositories, terminals and broker roots only; never real credentials or root mutation in tests. Require independent security review of the extended trust protocol.

## Safety-Stop Recovery

Preserve design choices, exact manifest/protocol state and remaining criteria before any fuse or permission stop. Continue via fixtures or a documented human-owned broker setup; never bypass a safety gate. Commit a verified increment before broad checks. Completion requires the one-ceremony positive path and all denial cases, not merely fewer prompts.

## Dispatch

Maintainer-requested implementation follow-up, auto-dispatch, tier:thinking. Own the security-sensitive design and implementation; do not expand the active #31289/#31290 bugfix PRs. No release authority is granted by this brief.

## Substantive comments (verbatim, in chronological order)

### Comment 1 — @marcusquinn at 2026-09-05T20:41:50Z

## Required design correction: no assumption of immediate human attendance

The user has now attempted approval of the regression-test source twice, including a freshly regenerated request, and both commands failed with `source-access request has expired; retry the blocked read`. Reissuing another short-lived request repeats the defect. This follow-up must solve delayed attendance, not just bundle more files into the same fragile approval flow.

### Implementation contract

1. Treat a pending request as a durable proposal with no access authority. Separate its lifecycle from the time-limited signed grant. The grant TTL starts on actual human approval, not request creation.
2. Provide a stable request/command that the human can use after hours or days without asking an active AI session to recreate it. At approval time, revalidate the exact repository, source manifest, file identity/digests, intended session/worktree and cancellation/revocation state before signing. Do not silently rebind changed bytes, a new session, or a broader manifest.
3. For elapsed proposal age alone, validate and approve the unchanged proposal in the same human ceremony. If the original request cannot safely be reused, the trusted human-facing broker should prepare and display the exact refreshed proposal in that invocation, requiring explicit confirmation of any changed scope rather than bouncing the human back to the assistant. Dead sessions and removed worktrees must produce a clear non-actionable/cancelled outcome or explicit new-context consent, never stale authorization.
4. Gather the full foreseeable protected-source set, including existing tests, before presenting the combined approval. Preserve previously granted valid capabilities; do not require the user to repeat successful approvals.
5. Keep pending proposals revocable and storage bounded without making ordinary delayed attendance fail. Cleanup must retain enough safe identity to explain or recover an old command, or use a stable broker-level request reference. Do not indefinitely retain source contents merely to keep a proposal usable.
6. Stop assistant-side expiry/reissue loops: persist the blocker and continuation, continue independent safe work, and report once. Never consume cached sudo or bypass the source guard as a convenience fix.

### Owning files and reference patterns

- `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py` and its imported source-access core: inspect proposal expiration checks, approval-time validation, proposal storage/cleanup, and grant TTL calculation; exact function names still require inspection.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-request.mjs`: stable request reuse and actionable delayed-approval messaging rather than repeated new IDs.
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh` and approval command integration already listed in the issue: preflight the source-and-test manifest and bind the intended worktree safely.
- Existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py` and `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-source-access-approval.mjs`: extend clock-controlled lifecycle fixtures, not new infrastructure.

### Additional acceptance and verification

- Advance a fake clock by 24 hours and 7 days after request creation. The same user-facing command must handle an unchanged valid proposal without an assistant retry and create a grant whose TTL starts at confirmation.
- Clock advancement does not rescue a revoked grant, approve substituted content, permit cross-session/worktree reuse, or confer any read permission before consent.
- Changed content, removed worktree, session termination, explicit cancellation, duplicate invocation, broker restart, and partial signing failures all have explicit safe outcomes; no automatic authority expansion.
- A batch containing the source file and its existing regression test requires one human decision, while unrelated files remain denied.
- Run the existing Python broker and Node source-access suites with these controlled-clock cases, the existing batch-approval/interactive-start tests, and independent security review before merge.

This is a user-requested correction to #31311's implementation scope, not a separate duplicate issue. The active inventory fix remains blocked until its current source permission exists; this design task must not bypass that gate.

# Keep primary Search exhaustion resource-scoped

## What

Prevent the small Search API allowance from imposing a global secondary cooldown
on unrelated REST and GraphQL work. Part of user-authorized productivity recovery
and release, following #31343 and #31348.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: invoke `_gh_secondary_cooldown_record_if_needed` with a
successful HTTP 200 response containing `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`,
`X-RateLimit-Resource: search`, no Retry-After and a reset that just elapsed.

**Actual output**: the shared state records `github-api-rate-limit-remaining-zero`
and adds a five-minute global cooldown. A live observation identified the producer
as `_rest_search_collect_items`; no secondary-limit or abuse response was present.

## How

Recognize only unambiguous primary Search exhaustion. Persist its actual reset in
a separate resource-scoped cooldown and enforce it before raw shim/REST search
calls. Other resources remain usable. Real secondary/abuse/Retry-After/429 and
unknown evidence retain the existing global fail-closed behavior. Never clear an
existing global cooldown or use status JSON as a quota grant.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh`

title: Stats wrapper starves later dashboards and times out during quality sweep
body:
## What

Make the stats wrapper complete successfully when the configured managed-repository set cannot be processed inside one scheduler deadline.

Health dashboards must be ordered fairly by their persisted refresh time, the optional repository pass must stop before exhausting cleanup time, and the daily quality sweep must resume across bounded per-repository batches.

## Why

An hourly installation with 21 pulse-enabled repositories repeatedly reached the 600-second wrapper ceiling and exited 124. Early dashboards refreshed repeatedly while a dashboard near the end of the configured list remained stale for 20 days. Once that dashboard was explicitly prioritized, the unbounded daily quality sweep consumed the remaining deadline and still caused exit 124.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep.sh`
- Existing focused shell tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`

### Complete Write Surface

- Add oldest-refresh-first health-dashboard ordering while preserving an explicit priority override.
- Check the remaining health-dashboard budget before starting another repository.
- Add persistent quality-sweep cursor state, a per-repository timeout, and aggregate-deadline cleanup reserve.
- Keep the daily completion timestamp unset until the resumable batch reaches all configured repositories.

### Implementation Steps

1. Order dashboard entries from missing/oldest refresh state to newest before applying the configured priority repository.
2. Stop optional dashboard iteration when the existing reserve check fails.
3. Rotate quality-sweep entries after the last attempted repository and persist the remaining count.
4. Bound each repository sweep, advance after a timeout, and finish the wrapper without turning expected partial work into a service failure.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Preserve Bash 3.2 compatibility and explicit function returns.
- Do not drop configured repositories or let one permanently starve later repositories.
- Preserve the existing explicit dashboard-priority override.
- Keep timeout and failure diagnostics visible in the stats log.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- Run ShellCheck on changed scripts.
- Run the existing health-dashboard, stats-wrapper timeout/headless, maintainer-guard, and quality-sweep serialization tests.
- Run `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`.
- Deploy with `setup.sh --non-interactive --stage agents` and verify a short live canary refreshes a dashboard, advances the quality cursor, logs `Finished`, and leaves the systemd timer active.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: Automated simplification tasks can conflict with their safety restrictions, causing repeated attempts and unfinished drafts
body:
## Description

Automated simplification tasks in a private project required removing every Qlty finding while also requiring "No public API changes". Workers identified parameter-count findings on existing public functions that could not be removed by the approaches considered without changing their calling contract. This is a task-design and recovery investigation, not a request to weaken safety checks or redesign working application code merely to satisfy a scanner.

## Observed Evidence

- One task accumulated 31 comments and five dispatches between 23:25 UTC September 5 and 00:06 UTC September 6, 2026, without an implementation.
- After two repeated blocker observations, its timeline recorded `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT active=true`. Three subsequent dispatches occurred. A later observation had the same blocker fingerprint but a different task revision; the final observation was classified `unknown` and explicitly imposed no global dispatch hold. What changed the revision is not established.
- Two other tasks produced partial draft PRs explicitly blocked by the same public-signature requirement conflict. Another draft remained unfinished after its worker exited blocked; that draft's precise blocker was not established.
- Two newer drafts still had active workers during the initial investigation and were not classified as abandoned.
- The configured worker maximum was six, with five implementation workers and one separate supervisor observed. This was not a demonstrated concurrency-limit violation.

## Expected Behavior and Design Considerations

Distinguish safe internal cleanup from changes to how other code calls a function. A scanner warning alone should not require a broader redesign. Consider allowing a justified retained finding, or preparing explicitly authorized caller-compatible migration work when worthwhile. Resolve conflicting task requirements rather than repeatedly dispatching workers against unchanged obstacles. Preserve unfinished drafts without merging incomplete work, but provide an explicit continuation or decline path. Manual safety holds must remain effective across scans and recovery.

## Reproducer

**Causal status: unconfirmed investigation.** Evidence is from live issue timelines and PR bodies, not a fresh reproducer on the latest release. Private identifiers and application filenames are intentionally omitted.

Inspection commands used: `gh issue view <issue> --repo <private-repo> --json body,comments,labels`; `gh pr list --repo <private-repo> --state open --json number,isDraft,body,statusCheckRollup`; `worker-activity-helper.sh live-workers`; `aidevops config get orchestration.max_workers_cap`.

A proposed isolated reproduction is a generated simplification task for a public function with excess explicit parameters, existing callers/tests, and both remove-all-findings and no-public-API-change requirements. Observe worker classification and subsequent dispatch eligibility without running repeated live paid attempts. No causal commit or complete owning-path trace has been proven.

## Investigation Scope and Verification

Inspect the simplification issue generator, blocker classification/revision invalidation, and draft-checkpoint continuation. Related upstream PR #31252 deliberately keeps unknown dossiers retryable and uses reason-aware revision invalidation; PR #31347 also changed Pulse recovery. Do not assume those fixes are absent or ineffective without verification. Exact implementation targets beyond the known framework components remain to be determined by maintainers.

Verify with existing generator and dispatch/blocker fixtures: compatible cleanup remains eligible; an unresolved API decision does not loop; unrelated changes do not spuriously resolve that decision; explicit manual holds block dispatch and continuation; incomplete drafts are never merged as completed repairs. Do not add broad restrictions on otherwise safe cleanup.

## Workarounds Applied

At the maintainer's explicit request, four affected tasks were left open, `auto-dispatch` was removed, and `no-auto-dispatch` plus `hold-for-review` were applied. A durable comment on each requires explicit maintainer permission to resume. No matching workers remained at the check. No application/framework code was edited, and no drafts were merged, closed, or deleted.

## Siblings

Task-generation policy, retry suppression, and orphaned-draft continuation may warrant separate follow-ups after maintainers establish ownership and distinguish already-fixed behavior. This report does not authorize speculative implementation or automatic dispatch.

## Environment

Observed attempts: aidevops v3.32.317, OpenCode v1.18.29, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Bash 5.2, GitHub CLI 2.100.0. Later diagnostics reported aidevops v3.32.318; behavior has not been re-triggered on that version. The operator prioritizes preserving working code and preventing repeated token expenditure.

title: Recover worker dependency reads through owned worktree provisioning
body:
## What

Keep worker dependency-read failures owned by AI using an in-worktree remediation path, without granting external-directory access or silently clearing signed permission holds.

## Evidence and root cause

A managed project worker stopped on external_directory/read while inspecting a dependency package outside its linked worktree. A separate worker requested external_directory/bash over an entire home directory; these are different risk classes and must not share a blanket approval remedy. Source inspection shows `_dlw_restore_worktree_deps` copies dependencies into a worker worktree, but `_dlw_skip_root_node_modules_restore` skips root node_modules by default. `_dlw_append_node_tool_env` adds canonical bin paths, which does not solve dependency source reads. `_bootstrap_aidevops_worktree_js_deps` intentionally avoids running user-project installation lifecycle scripts. Private project identities and paths are deliberately omitted; reproduce with fixtures.

## Relationship to existing work

Open #31305 covers general scope/integration recovery and #31311 covers separately signed protected-source consent. This narrower dependency-provisioning and deny-with-remediation producer/consumer path is not implemented by either brief. Reuse their ownership/continuation contracts; do not create a new general permission protocol or duplicate their coordinator.

## Initial implementation map

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`: `_dlw_restore_worktree_deps`, root restore decision and node tool environment.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`: existing constrained dependency bootstrap.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs` and `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`: inspect exact deny/pause and continuation semantics before proposing recovery.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`: preserved checkpoint and permission holds.
- `.agents/reference/dispatch-blockers.md`: document bounded remediation versus genuinely required new authority.
- Existing permission broker/helper tests and dispatch/worktree fixtures. Locate exact dependency fixture filenames during implementation; unknown additional test paths are not permission to invent interfaces.

## Required behavior and safety

1. Prefer supported controller-side dependency provisioning before starting the worker. Make required dependency sources readable inside the owned worktree without a shared canonical-directory grant. Reuse existing copy machinery and make resource cost explicit; do not blindly copy every repository's multi-GB root on each attempt.
2. Validate repository, lockfile/package identity, destination ownership and link containment. Reject symlink traversal and credential-bearing paths. Do not install packages or execute lifecycle scripts under newly invented authority.
3. If a worker already paused, first prove the original process is terminal or explicitly hand off its ownership. Preserve commits, checkpoint PR identity, exact original request and audit evidence. A denied tool must not be retried under an implied grant.
4. Where current contracts permit a trusted controller to supply an in-boundary alternative, resume the exact checkpoint with that alternative and leave the rejected capability ungranted. If no authorized supersession path exists, report that limitation precisely and integrate via the existing coordinator contract; do not remove a permission label or synthesize approval to get dispatch working.
5. Broad execution requests, credential access and genuinely new external authority remain held. Repeated unchanged dependency evidence produces one owned recovery action, not comment storms or replacement workers.

## Verification

Use fixture repositories and fake GitHub/permission envelopes only. Cover root restore disabled, bounded successful in-worktree dependency reads, pnpm-style links, missing/stale package identity, copied source containment, missing dependencies, foreign/live owner, preserved checkpoint, repeated event deduplication, and broad external bash denial. Run existing test-permission-broker.mjs, test-worker-permission-helper.sh, affected dispatch fixtures and ShellCheck. Independent security review is required for any changed permission or ownership boundary.

## Dispatch

Worker-ready high-priority framework follow-up, thinking tier. The objective is safe autonomous remediation, not bypassing the existing permission system. No publication or live permission grants are authorized by this issue.

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Bundle approved issue acceptance with bounded protected-source access

## What

Remove the redundant second human authorization interruption when a maintainer approves an issue and immediately starts implementation. Provide one explicit human ceremony that separately approves the issue and an exact, signed protected-source manifest for the intended implementation context.

The source grant is a narrow, independently verifiable capability; issue approval alone never becomes blanket source or secret-read authority. A valid bundled manifest must be consumed by both the CLI verification path and the OpenCode read hook for every exact approved path in its intended session and linked worktree.

## Why

During #31289, `approval-helper.sh verify issue` returned `VERIFIED` with proven locked continuity and the interactive entrypoint had claimed the issue and created its worktree. Reading tracked `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` was nevertheless blocked solely for its secret-bearing basename, requiring another signed source approval although no credential values were needed for inventory cleanup.

Related work #30567 / PR #30573 added multi-file source manifests, and #31035 / PR #31040 preserves permission across verified same-session direct edits. Reuse those capabilities rather than duplicating or weakening them. Neither joins initial issue approval with source approval nor safely hands authority to a newly created implementation worktree.

The current short-lived request model also fails delayed attendance: a user attempted approval twice, including for a freshly regenerated request, but both returned `source-access request has expired; retry the blocked read`. Reissuing short-lived requests repeats the defect and can lead to assistant-side expiry/reissue loops.

Finally, live evidence showed a two-path manifest was approved and `aidevops source-access verify` returned `VERIFIED` for both paths in the intended session/worktree, yet OpenCode Read calls reported no approval and generated per-path requests. Per-path approval subsequently enabled immutable snapshot delivery, proving that hook lookup—not the files themselves—ignored the bundled grant.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-commands.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/source-access-helper.py`
